title: Deep learning image reconstruction algorithms in low-dose radiation abdominal computed tomography: assessment of image quality and lesion diagnostic confidence.
summary: Deep-learning image reconstruction was compared with FBP and ASiR-V in phantom and clinical low-dose abdominal CT, improving image quality and lesion diagnostic confidence.
ai_technology: DLIR at low, medium and high settings reconstructed low-dose abdominal CT images for phantom and clinical assessment.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: DLIR improved noise texture and image quality relative to FBP/ASiR-V; DL-M had the best balance of image quality and lesion diagnostic confidence.
evidence.unknown: Phantom measurements plus prospective clinical study, radiologist Likert assessments and signal/noise metrics provide direct bounded validation.
evidence.ai_role: DLIR at low, medium and high settings reconstructed low-dose abdominal CT images for phantom and clinical assessment.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
